I work in the oil industry on a production platform in the gulf. While I am not a pipe fitter we have a construction crew that has them and I have worked around. To the best of my knowledge they will measure and cut the material then prepare it to be welded. When the job doesn't call for this they will be given other tasks such as painting over the welds or fire watch or what ever is needed. They will rig up loads to be lifted by the crane and of course stage, unload, and load their equipment. They work on a 14 x 14 schedule so they only work half the year. I also know they have some construction crews that don't work on a set schedule.

I am a millwright. I work with a pipefitter. What was it about millwrighting that you found off putting? All of your questions depend on your employer. If you are a private contractor, work for a contracting out company, or work directly for a company will change all of the answers. If you are unionized will affect your rate of pay and hours. Variety of work is very slim, but again it all depends on where you work. The pipefitter I work with has retired from one plant, and now works casually (2 days a week) at my plant. As far as maintenance, we live in a replacement world. It makes more financial sense to replace parts than rebuild them.

Hey I found a Millwright!

What turned me off of Millwrights is the hours. I know my body's limits. I have pushed them too hard before and have been stuck recovering for two years.

I have done the work 12 hours a day, no breaks, nonstop for months. I do not want to break myself and go through what I have again. It seems Millwrights have a 12+ hour workday as a rule, not an exception. I won't be able to keep up. I would crash and burn before my apprenticeship would be up. It is not about work ethic, I will work my ass off for 8 - 10 hours and the occasional 12+, but I have hypersomnia now... I get exhausted after a long shift and will be useless without adequate sleep.

What gave me the most input into this was this post: https://www.reddit.com/r/millwrights/comments/3pzqvi/for_the_people_considering_becoming_a_millwright/

My concerns from reading it are

I've worked 7 days a week at 12hrs a day for 4 months, i've had no work for 14 months straight.

The longest shift ive worked is 23hrs straight.

The hours along with the downtime between work (more than a month a half sometimes) are my deciding factors for being a Millwright. Nothing else in that post bothered me.

On a different note, it sure is a replacement world. In terms of the Unions, there is not much in terms of a career in repair, it is a majority of new installations. I was looking forward to being the guy to fix shit! Oh well.

What does the pipefitter you work with do if he is working casually 2 days a week?

I work 8 hours a day 5 days a week. there is unlimited overtime available of it want the cash. depending on the job, I get regular (and extended) breaks. if something important is broken, I'll push a little harder. the extremes that guy posted are voluntary. our pipefitter works on emergency sprinkler systems, plumbing, and our regular water systems, whether that is for lubrication of equipment or anything else is up to the millwrights once it reaches its destination.
